content:
According to Bloomberg's latest report, Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop. The company is reportedly "developing prototypes," but has not yet decided whether to ultimately launch this product.

The internal prototypes reportedly feature "a slim fabric strap with a sensor-equipped computing module." The project is currently in the "technology exploration" phase, and Bloomberg indicates the product will not be launched until at least 2028, if Apple ultimately decides to release it.

The project is said to have the support of Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took over Apple's health team last October after Jeff Williams departed.

Products such as Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among users who want to track health and fitness without wearing a smartwatch. According to Reuters, Oura is preparing for an IPO, and recently announced that it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ending June 30; in the nine months ending June 30, revenue grew 74%, reaching $1.21 billion.

However, Apple still dominates the smartwatch market. The Apple Watch also offers far richer functionality than health-and-fitness-focused wearables such as Oura and Whoop.
